children: Iraq is speeding up procedures to launch a major project involving the construction of oil pipelines to Turkey and Syria, the oil ministry has reported.
The pipelines have a capacity of nearly 2.2 million barrels per day (bpd) and will allow Iraq to export crude via Turkey and Syria away from the Strait of Hormuz.

Oil Minister Bassim Khudair, who headed a meeting to discuss the project at the weekend, directed officials to “accelerate the technical and commercial arrangements and finalise preparations ahead of the contract signing,” the ministry said.
The proposed pipelines would run from the southern oil hub of Basra through Haditha to Fishkhabour in northern Iraq.

A separate section would connect Haditha with Baniyas on Syria’s Mediterranean coast.Iraq, OPEC’s second largest oil producer, exported nearly 3.4 million bpd through Hormuz before the war between Iran and the US erupted in late February.
(Writing by N Saeed; Editing by Anoop Menon)
